content_text: external validation isn't just an addiction or weakness of character to buff out, it's a prerequisite for progressing to the highest levels of the game. think about it. >if you're elon musk, how many people do you have each day telling, you, "hey man, you did an excellent job today?" A: zero >as you get higher and higher in the world, excellence is no longer noteworthy, but expected additionally, the level of criticism directed your way rises in linear fashion with the height you occupy so at the highest levels, you are dealing with 99.9% vociferous criticism, and maybe 0.01% "nice work today today" so the removal of external validation as a driver isn't just "morally right" or "good to undertake," it is an imperative to get to the top and remain at the top trust me, musk, bezos, these types are not even listening to the praise and criticism of the mob bezos, kobe, they're not driven by what the fickle and ever-changing opinions of fans and media. they have to be driven entirely by the courage of their own conviction...and their own, as Montaigne references, system for evaluating their own conduct in a vacuum the sooner you can re-orient yourself to operate this way - motivated by intrinsic and not extrinsic factors - the better the odds are that you will reach the top and stay there. this swing factor on its own (overly sensitive to external validation + praise + criticism) is a hard roadblock that prevents many from progressing to the highest levels of the game all stems from self-respect, self-belief, knowledge of self, a trusted group of advisors, and a general but finely-honed calibrator as to "what matters" re feedback, and what is just crabs in a bucket. ask anyone "at the top" and they will echo this. "I wake up in the morning, look in the mirror," says Waren Buffett, "and after that, everyone's had their say." This is the only functional way to operate when u are in sole possession of the #1 seed...
